newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - March 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - March 12.

text.p: The following stories appeared in Wednesday's Daily Variety:

* HOLLYWOOD - A consortium of lenders led by Chase Manhattan Bank has filed notice of default on DreamWorks' proposed Playa Vista project. The notice means the Chase-led consortium, which includes Bank of America and Sanwa Bank, could foreclose on the project or initiate a bank sale after 110 days. The loans involved total about $150 million plus interest, according to sources.

* NEW YORK - Paramount Pictures and PolyGram Filmed Entertainment are negotiating a three-year, co-financing arrangement which would encompass an estimated 10 to 12 big-budget films, sources said. The deal is expected to include a third party. Sources close to the negotiations said that the deal is not expected to be finalized until the summer. Polygram has entered into discussions with South Korean investors for outside financing -- said to be 20 percent -- of the overall slate.

* WASHINGTON - President Clinton said broadcasters should be required to give free airtime to politicians as a condition of their digital TV licenses and, in an unusual move, publicly called on the Federal Communications Commission to make his wish come true.

* HOLLYWOOD - Procter & Gamble has signed an overall production-distribution deal with Sony's Columbia TriStar Television Group. The three-year deal, which runs through the 1999-2000 TV season, will look to develop programming for primetime, daytime and firstrun syndication. The alliance is Procter & Gamble's second partnership with a major Hollywood studio. P&G is in the third year of a similar deal with Viacom's Paramount.

* NEW YORK - Westinghouse's CBS has rolled into first for the March 3-9 primetime Nielsens week, helped along by a record "Touched by an Angel" and a strong start for its revamped Monday lineup. General Electric's NBC led the week in adults 18-49 and 25-54. Combined with the previous week's tie with NBC, CBS earned a share of first for a second week in a row, something it hadn't accomplished since November 1994. There's still work to be done demographically, though -- CBS finished the week fourth among many key audience segments, including its target demo, adults 25-54.

* HOLLYWOOD - Rob Lowe has a two-year deal with Paramount Network Television to develop a comedy series with the studio. Lowe, best known for his feature work, has received good reviews for his portrayal of a deaf mute in the ABC miniseries "The Stand."
